I will keep my land arranged around labor, water, and steady income. I have 18 mu total, and because my household has some off-farm work, I will not make the plan too complicated or too labor-heavy. I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on the main block because it is the safest and most familiar system for my conditions in Quzhou County, and I have well irrigation to support stable grain production. I will put 10 mu into wheat followed by maize on the same land. That gives me food grain, cash flow, and lower risk. On the remaining 8 mu, I will split between chili and cotton. I will keep 4 mu of chili because chili can bring cash if managed well, but it needs more water, fertilizer, and spraying, so I will not expand it too much. I will keep 4 mu of cotton because I already know how to manage it, it spreads risk, and it fits my labor better than expanding chili too far. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it matters most, keep fertilizer at moderate but not low levels, and rely on irrigation mainly for wheat, maize, and chili when the season turns dry. I will not chase extreme input use. I want stable yields, manageable labor, and lower risk across the whole year.
